name: Fushimi Inari Taisha
desc: Ten thousand vermilion gates climbing a mountain, open all night, totally free. Broke-traveler royalty.

name: Kinkaku-ji
desc: A pavilion wrapped in actual gold, doubled in its own pond. Costs less than the latte you'd sip describing it.

name: Kiyomizu-dera
desc: A wooden stage jutting over the maple canopy. In autumn it burns red and so does your camera roll.

name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove
desc: Green corridors that creak and hush in the wind. Go at dawn and you own the entire soundtrack.

name: Nishiki Market
desc: A 400-year-old food alley — pickles, skewers, matcha everything. Grazing absolutely counts as dinner.

name: Gion District
desc: Lantern-lit lanes where a geiko might glide past. Look, don't chase — the vibe itself is the ticket.

name: Philosopher's Path
desc: A canal-side stroll purpose-built for overthinking. Cherry blossoms in April, perfect quiet the rest of the year.

name: Ryoan-ji
desc: Fifteen rocks, raked gravel, and a silence that quietly rearranges your brain. Cheapest therapy in town.

name: Nijo Castle
desc: A shogun's palace with nightingale floors that chirp on purpose — a medieval intruder alarm you get to test.

name: Ginkaku-ji
desc: The 'silver' pavilion that never got its silver — and is somehow more beautiful for the broken promise.
